## What to build

Preserve contextual-share dependency refusals when a statically resolvable indirect call removes a lexical binding or reparents a lookup environment. The same visible scope mutation must have the same dependency meaning as its directly named counterpart.

On main snapshot `339315c387f31deace77566f5d3294b15b323865`, summarize two rows with grouping values a and b and measure values one and three. Define an earlier ordinary summary, temporarily shadow its name inside a share source, remove the temporary binding, and read that name again. Direct removal is correctly refused. Resolving the base removal function through a literal-name lookup instead is accepted and returns source values one, three and four with Total shares one-quarter, three-quarters and one, despite the prohibited dependency on the earlier summary.

The other dependency direction also bypasses refusal: an ordinary summary after a share reads input payload values 100 and 300 while the displayed share alias contains one-quarter, three-quarters and one. Indirect parent-environment setters similarly allow an environment treated as external during planning to inherit from the summary mask during evaluation. Direct setters are correctly refused.

The bounded reproductions cover Parent and Total shares, both dependency directions, literal-target get/match.fun/getFunction calls and do.call targets. These callees are already explicitly resolved elsewhere in dependency analysis; this does not request inference of arbitrary opaque callback effects. Closed #1042 and #1045 repaired nested removals and visible reparenting respectively, but their scope-effect checks missed these already resolvable call forms. Both effects fit one independently verifiable ticket because they must apply the existing callee-resolution boundary consistently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Refuse the demonstrated source-to-earlier-ordinary-alias and later-ordinary-to-earlier-share dependencies for both Parent and Total shares.
- [ ] Cover indirectly resolved rm/remove calls and parent-environment mutation, including the supported literal-target resolver and do.call forms.
- [ ] Preserve genuinely retained lexical bindings, stable external lookups, non-inheriting lookups, unrelated mutations, and caller-shadowed functions according to ordinary lookup.
- [ ] Keep unresolved mask-capable lookups conservative without executing arbitrary caller expressions during analysis or adding an opaque-side-effect inference promise.
- [ ] Preserve ordinary evaluation without contextual shares and lazy construction; add focused public-interface regressions and pass the Package-affecting Review-ready check.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

[Dated investigation, minimized reproduction and executable replay evidence](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/1adc767d37bf97288b8a00da16f0ae8cc027c4f8/investigation/summary-grouping-total-share-bughunt-2026-10-31.md#f2-resolved-mutation-callees-did-not-carry-their-scope-effects). Recorded in PR #1098, which contains investigation material only.
